01 Who We Are

Our history

Where the name comes from, and the people who built it.

We are immensely proud of our long-standing history and trusted reputation in India. Our success is a testament to the visionary leadership of the late Dr. Krishna Kumar Birla, whose influence has left an indelible mark on the growth and development of the country. Our name, which draws inspiration from the majestic Zuari river flowing through Goa, embodies its essence and its significance in the lives of millions.

Dr. K.K. Birla
(1918–2008)
The Zuari River, Goa — after which the company is named

Our present

Today, the Group is led by Mr. Saroj Kumar Poddar, who took over the legacy in 2008. In 2011, the individual companies operating in separate envelopes were brought together to synergise the valuable equities of each. Over the last 12 years, Adventz Group has diversified and grown across the key drivers of the Indian economy — today operating in four industry verticals: Agrochemicals, Engineering & Infrastructure, Lifestyle & Real Estate, and Services, through subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures. The Group continues to partner with world leaders and deepen its engagement with consumers across the value spectrum.

Mr. Saroj Kumar Poddar
Chairman, Adventz Group

A legacy of 50+ years

The milestones that shaped the Group.

1967
Zuari Agro Chemicals Limited (ZACL)

Founded by the late Dr. K.K. Birla, in financial and technical collaboration with House of Birlas, Armour & Co., Chicago, U.S.A, IFC and Bank of America. Plant commissioned in 1973.

1994
Chambal Fertilisers & Chemicals Ltd. (CFCL)

New urea plant commissioned in Rajasthan under CFCL, installed with a per-day capacity of 1.1 MT.

1995
Major developments

Indian Furniture Products Ltd (IFPL): set up in technical collaboration with Group Serbio, France, in Chennai. Simon India Ltd: set up as SIL, 50:50 JV with Simon Carves of United Kingdom. Zuari Seeds Ltd: set up for production and trading of hybrid seeds.

1998
Zuari Industries Ltd.

ZACL was renamed to ZIL to reflect a diversified business portfolio.

1999
CFCL expansion

Commissioning of second plant (Gadepan-II) with enhanced capacity of 1,520 MTPD of ammonia and 2,620 MTPD of urea.

2000
Zuari Indian Oil Tanking

Set up as a JV between Zuari Industries Ltd and Indian Oil Tanking Ltd to provide terminal services for the supply of petroleum products.

2002
Paradeep Phosphates Ltd. (PPL)

Acquired Paradeep Phosphates through a JV between ZIL and OCP, Morocco – Zuari Maroc Phosphates Pvt Ltd (ZMPPL).

2007
Zuari Rotem Speciality

A JV project producing state-of-the-art, zero-waste, water-soluble fertilisers, improving yield by 15–30% compared to conventional fertilisers.

2008
Legacy continues

Mr. Saroj K. Poddar took the baton from Dr. K.K. Birla and continues his legacy as the Chairman.

2009
Zuari Infraworld India Ltd (ZIIL)

Set up for foraying into the real estate development business. Major projects include Zuari Rainforest – Goa, Zuari Garden City – Mysore and Saint Regis – Dubai.

2011
Foundation of Adventz Group

Formed to bring synergies of the diversified business under one umbrella for both Zuari Industries Ltd & Texmaco Rail & Engineering Ltd.

2012
ZIL demerger

ZIL demerged into ZACL (fertiliser business/undertaking) and ZGL (non-fertiliser businesses).

2015
Mangalore Chemicals & Fertilizers Limited (MCFL)

Acquisition of MCF Limited and Zuari Rotem Speciality Fertilisers, becoming a 100% subsidiary of ZACL.

2017
Fabyki Mebli Forte

Entered into a JV with Fabyki Mebli Forte, Poland — leased out assets of IFPL to FFPL.

2022
Major milestones

ZGL–GSML merger: merger of ZGL and GSML, renamed ZGL as ZIL by scheme. Paradeep Phosphates Limited: public listing of PPL; sale of ZACL's assets in Goa to PPL.

2023
Zuari Envien Bioenergy Pvt Ltd

ZIL and Envien Group collaborated to develop a 180 KLPD grain-based distillery in Aira, Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, with plans to scale up ethanol production to ~1,000 KLPD.

The training period lasts 12 months, and probation lasts 6 months. Your manager provides feedback following one-to-one discussions with you, and HR reviews the manager's feedback and recommendations before confirmation.

POSH — preventing sexual harassment

Our commitment to a safe, respectful workplace.

Zero tolerance. Any unwelcome behaviour of a sexual nature that makes someone feel uncomfortable, intimidated, or offended — verbal, non-verbal, physical, or visual — has no place here.

Types of sexual harassment

Quid pro quo: offering benefits or making threats in exchange for sexual favours.

Hostile work environment: creating an intimidating, offensive or hostile atmosphere.

Online harassment: through digital platforms, including emails, messages or social media.

How to report

We encourage prompt, confidential reporting of any incident. A designated committee receives and addresses complaints, and support is provided to those affected throughout the process. Reported incidents are investigated thoroughly and impartially; substantiated allegations lead to appropriate disciplinary action, and confidentiality is maintained for all parties.

Prevention

Regular awareness training on rights and responsibilities, and a culture that promotes mutual respect, diversity and inclusion.

Why it matters

Beyond the legal consequences for both the harasser and the organisation, harassment damages reputation and erodes employee morale, productivity and retention. Every employee plays a part in preventing it and fostering a culture of respect.

Quick tips for you

Seven functions you'll interact with often — what each one does, how it works, and who to go to. Jump to any of them from the sidebar.

Know Your Customer (KYC)

Onboards and verifies clients. Handles new registrations, modifications, Re-KYC, and CKYC/KRA updates so every account meets SEBI, NSDL, CDSL and PMLA requirements before it trades.

Depository Participant (DP)

Services holdings once an account is live. Its core job is transmission — moving securities to the rightful surviving holder, nominee, or legal heir when an account holder passes away.

RMS

Keeps trading within safe limits. Calculates margins and collateral, pledges and unpledges stock, and squares off positions that breach ageing-debit or shortage rules.

Broking Operations

Runs the back office. The Netbackoffice system handles client ledgers, billing, and reports, while the team manages payment collection, CTCL dealer IDs, and RM/Dealer changes.

Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)

The registry of record for every shareholder. Manages dematerialization, transfers and transmissions, corporate actions, ISIN generation, and end-to-end investor servicing.

Customer Experience

The single point of contact for clients. Owns every query end to end — from first raise through WeCare to resolution — so branches and clients deal with one team, not five.

HR & Admin

Your people partner from day one. Owns everything from payroll and leave to hiring, onboarding, and facilities — the team behind a smooth, well-supported employee experience.

KYC — Know Your Customer

Onboarding, verification, and regulatory compliance

What the department does

Key responsibilities

Verification of customer KYC documents · online and offline KYC processing · CKYC registration and updates · KRA registration, modification, and status updates · KYC modifications (name, address, PAN, mobile, email, bank details, nominee) · Re-KYC processing · FATCA/CRS declaration verification.

DP Finance activities managed by KYC

Debit Note processing · Credit Note processing · payment updates · refund processing for closed accounts — all under SEBI, NSDL, CDSL and PMLA guidelines.

The KYC Operations team ensures regulatory compliance, a seamless onboarding experience, and accurate customer records — while also managing DP Finance activities like debit notes, credit notes, and refunds.

How a KYC request flows

Receive the KYC or modification request (online or offline).
Verify supporting documents, including PAN and Aadhaar where applicable.
Process the request through internal systems.
Update records on the KRA and CKYC portals.
Confirm approval and maintain customer records.

When to contact KYC

New KYC registration · KYC modification or Re-Activation requests · KRA and CKYC updates · Re-KYC processing · KYC rejection clarification · Debit Note / Credit Note queries · payment update requests · refund processing for closed accounts · KRA/CKYC portal issues.

DP — Depository Participant

Holdings, account servicing, and transmission of securities

DP is the custodian layer between a client's demat holding and the depositories — NSDL and CDSL. Once an account is opened and KYC is cleared, DP takes over servicing the holding itself: dematerialisation and rematerialisation of shares, pledges, and — most critically — transmission of securities to the rightful holder, nominee, or legal heir when an account holder passes away. In short, DP makes sure every holding stays accurately recorded and legally accounted for, for as long as the client stays invested.

Procedure for transmission of securities

When an account holder passes away, securities are transmitted to the rightful surviving holder, nominee, or legal heir. There are four scenarios, each with its own process and form.

A. Jointly held securities

The surviving client(s) request transmission of the balance to their own account. If the surviving client is the first holder, only the Joint Holder Transmission Form is needed. If the first holder is the deceased, a new Account Opening Form must also be signed.

B. Nomination made on Annexure JA

On the death of the sole client (or all clients), the nominee(s) submit an application — the Nominee Transmission Form — to transmit the securities to their own account.

C. Legal heir(s) — holding value under ₹15 lakh

The legal heir(s) or claimant(s) request the Participant to transmit the deceased's balances to their account, using the Legal Heir Transmission Form.

D. Legal heir(s) — holding value over ₹15 lakh

Same process as above — Legal Heir Transmission Form — with additional scrutiny given the higher value involved.

Mandatory documents in every case

Notarised Death Certificate, signed by the claimant(s), with the original seen and verified by the branch official.
PAN of the deceased, duly signed by the claimant(s).
Self-attested PAN & Aadhaar of the claimant(s).
CML extracted from the NSDL/CDSL online system, stamped and signed by the target DP, self-attested by the claimant(s). Not required if the target demat account is already with us.
Documents are first collected at the branch and sent to Head Office for verification. If there's a discrepancy — name/address mismatch, missing nomination on Annexure JA, missing family declaration or ration card, or transactions after the account holder's death — a separate indemnity bond is required for each discrepancy, in addition to the standard documents. If a witness signs the indemnity bond, their self-attested ID proof must accompany it.
If the CML is digitally signed by the target DP, share it by email as well, for DSC verification purposes.

RMS — Risk Management System

Limits, margins, collateral, and square-off rules

RMS is the safety net that keeps every trade within acceptable risk. Once a client starts trading, RMS sets and monitors margin and collateral requirements in real time, tracks exposure across cash and derivatives, and steps in with a square-off the moment a position breaches its limit or a shortage runs past its allowed window. It's the function that protects both the client and the firm from unchecked risk — quietly running in the background on every single trade.

Collateral allocation

Collateral splits into two types — Cash and Non-Cash — each with its own onward chain.

Cash

Cash itself, or Cash Equivalents — SGB (Sovereign Gold Bond) and Liquid Bees. Liquid Bees flow onward as Repledge Stock.

Non-Cash

Exchange Approved Stocks, which become Pledge Stock and then Repledge Stock.

Collateral stock is considered only after applying the appropriate haircut.

Limit calculation

BOD Limit = Ledger Balance + Approved Re-pledged Stock Amount

During the day, EPN (Early Pay-in) is added on request. New stock re-pledge updates during the day, and the fund pay-out amount is adjusted accordingly. Check scrip margin anytime in ODIN with Shift + F7 (Security Information window), and view your limits and net positions from the RMS menu → Limits Set / Net Position.

Margin shortage — possible reasons

MTM loss

Margin increment by Exchange

Stock haircut increased by Exchange

Stock moved to Trade-to-Trade or un-approved category

Collateral benefit reduced or removed by Exchange

Physical Delivery Margin / Commodity Tender Margin, or a removed hedge position

Restricted scrips — equity

Margin / Intraday block

T, TS, Z, ZP, BE, X, XT, M, MT, GSM · IRP, Call Auction/illiquid scrip, F, P, P(n), etc. Scrips blocked here cannot be traded intraday.

Delivery block

Lot size >1, price <₹1 and market cap <₹50 Cr · X, XT, MT, SM, ST group. Scrips blocked here cannot be squared off intraday/same day by default.

Additional Surveillance Deposit Margin (ASD) applies on GSM 2–6 and IBC 1–2. T, TS, Z, ZP, BE, XT, M, MT limits are available as per the client's ledger balance.

Restricted scrips — derivatives & commodities

NFO blocks apply when: option price moves ±15% · expiry is beyond 75 days · LTP moves ±20% for liquid stock F&O, or ±6% for liquid index F&O · open interest is under 2,000 · on physical delivery on expiry day · during the tender period in commodities · or when the Exchange itself blocks the F&O scrip.

FO ban

Each day, the Exchange checks whether aggregate open interest in any scrip's futures & options exceeds 95% of the market-wide position limit. If it does, clients/TMs may only trade to decrease positions until open interest falls back to 80% or below. Ban details are emailed to branches each morning by RMS and are viewable on branch ODIN terminals — only square-off of open positions is allowed, and violations attract exchange penalties.

Margins in derivatives & commodities

Up-front margin required = Initial (SPAN) margin + Exposure margin + Premium + other charges, if any. MTM loss margin must be collected by T+1. At least 50% of the margin should be in the form of cash. Other margin types: Physical Delivery Margin, Commodity Tender/Delivery Margin, Additional Margin, and Special Commodity Margin.

Physical delivery margin — how it builds up

Applies mainly to long (buy) In-The-Money (ITM) stock options that are held to expiry and settled by actual delivery of shares, not cash. It's made up of VAR Margin (potential losses over a set time), ELM (Extreme Loss Margin for volatile swings), and Ad hoc Margin (extra buffer the exchange may require). Use the NSE margin calculator to find the exact Total Delivery Margin.

Days to expiry% of Total Delivery Margin required
T-4 days10%
T-3 days25%
T-2 days45%
T-1 day70%
T day (Expiry)100%
Example: for +500 buy positions of a Reliance 2500 Call expiring 30th October with a Total Delivery Margin of ₹1,92,961.67 — you'd need ₹19,296.17 (10%) in your ledger by T-4 days, rising to the full amount by expiry.

Margin pledging of stock

Clients or branches can initiate a margin pledge request two ways:

A. Through Zuarimoney (App, Web, Diet)

The client initiates the pledge directly — the system redirects them to NSDL for authentication.

B. Through the Back-office team

Back-office initiates the pledge; the client authenticates via an NSDL SMS with OTP and details; back-office then confirms status and sends it for re-pledge to the Clearing Corporation (CC).

The limit becomes available only after successful re-pledge confirmation is received from the Clearing Corporation (CC).

T5 ageing debit collection & square-off

T5 intimation is sent to the branch by email each morning; clients get SMS/email reminders on T3, T4 and T5 based on the ageing debit amount.
The branch must collect the full amount — elimination of small debits is not allowed.
Unclear instruments (e.g. cheques not cleared by 12:00 PM on T5) don't count as collections and must be squared off.
Unpaid stocks are squared off before 1:00 PM, with each client informed of the liquidation via recorded lines.

Detailed information is viewable through the PCR report on branch/RM/client login. Exchange and regulatory requirements apply with no deviations.

MTF shortage collection & square-off

Shortage carried more than 3 days → squared off by the 4th day.

Shortage more than 125% → squared off the same day.

Shortage from a stock moving out of the approved list → same day if >125%, otherwise by the 4th day.

Uncertain market volatility → immediate square-off.

Stock early pay-in

Early pay-in (EPN) is processed five times a day, at approximately 10:00 AM, 11:00 AM, 12:00 PM, after due settlement stock payout (1:00–1:30 PM), and 2:30 PM — each batch takes roughly 30–45 minutes to execute. 100% of the sell-stock benefit is allowed once EPN is successfully received.

Clients can avail early pay-in benefit for stock sold in delivery from DP/CUSPA, but cannot buy back stock sold in delivery unless they have sufficient margin at the time of selling. BTST early pay-in is available only after the stock is received from the Clearing Corporation (CC), and the EPN benefit is applied per branch/client request.

Other RMS processes

Fund Payout · Stock Un-Pledge · CTCL Activation/Modification/Deactivation · Client's Mapping · Volume Emails · Daily BOD email for T5, Urgent Action & MTF Shortage · Derivative Shortage.

04 IT — Do's & Don'ts

IT induction — new employee

The Zuari Finserv IT Department is committed to giving you the tools and support to work securely and efficiently. Please read and follow these guidelines.

Your IT resources

Company laptop/desktop and accessories · official Zimbra Mail / Microsoft 365 email · access to required business applications · Local Drive/OneDrive/SharePoint/NAS for file storage · VPN access, if applicable.

Password & MFA

Create a strong password (minimum 12 characters). Never share it with anyone. Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Report any suspected account compromise immediately.

Email & internet usage

Use your company email for official business only. Don't open suspicious emails, links, or attachments. Access only authorized websites and business applications.

Information security

Keep company information confidential. Lock your computer when away from your desk. Save work files only to approved storage (OneDrive/SharePoint) — never copy company data to personal devices or cloud storage.

AI tools

Don't upload confidential company, customer, financial, or business information to public AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) unless specifically approved.

Software installation

Install only software approved by the IT Department. Never disable antivirus or other security controls.

Report lost/stolen devices, phishing emails, malware alerts, and unauthorized access to the IT Helpdesk immediately.

Quick do's & don'ts

✅ Do's

  • Use company IT assets for official work only
  • Use strong passwords and enable MFA
  • Lock your computer when away from your desk
  • Save company files only in approved locations
  • Keep your system updated
  • Report security incidents immediately
  • Follow IT and Information Security policies
  • Keep company assets secure

❌ Don'ts

  • Don't share your password or MFA codes
  • Don't install unauthorized software or browser extensions
  • Don't connect unknown USB devices
  • Don't upload company data to public AI tools without approval
  • Don't use personal email or cloud storage for company files
  • Don't click suspicious links or email attachments
  • Don't disable antivirus or security settings
  • Don't leave your laptop unattended or unlocked
